per_pair.why: Both use simple radial bursts; B has slightly more refined pixel consistency but fundamentally similar approach.
A's death burst is nearly invisible—just a few fading particles; B has a crafted multi-layer golden explosion with clear animation arc and visual feedback.
A's spawn is nearly invisible; B has elaborate golden bursts with dotted ring overlays and layered particle emergence across all 12 frames.

loser_biggest_gap: Death burst lacks any punchy feedback—add a golden explosion burst with particle debris and a clear timing arc (fast pop into slower decay) to match B's impact and visual presence.
loser_other_gaps: Spawn effect is too minimal; needs layered circular bursts with colored outlines and particle trails to feel alive
Color palette is monochromatic (beige/cream); add gold, orange, or other warm accent colors for visual richness and readability
Hit-spark needs slightly more refined animation frames to feel as polished as B's progression
reasoning: B delivers substantially more crafted and punchy effects across the set. The death burst and spawn effects are night-and-day differences in visual craft, layering, color choice, and animation sophistication. A's effects feel like placeholders—minimal particles, no color variation, no clear animation arcs. B shows industry-standard polish: deliberate timing (quick peaks into slow decays), thoughtful color (golden/warm tones), and multi-element layering that guides the eye and communicates feedback. The spawn in particular shows the most decisive gap: B's golden rings and particle layers create presence and anticipation; A's spawn is nearly invisible.
